security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from documentation examples, Markdown code spans, placeholder API keys, and intended MCP networking guidance. The real risk is the included evaluation runner, which can launch a user-selected stdio MCP command with supplied environment variables. No prompt injection attempt or hidden exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Evaluation runner can launch arbitrary stdio commands with supplied environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run the evaluation script only against trusted commands, and consider adding an allowlist or confirmation prompt before subprocess launch.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes many placeholder API keys and remote URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all examples clearly marked as placeholders and remind users not to paste real secrets into shared files or evaluation XML.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation fetching is part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users when external documentation will be fetched and encourage reviewing URLs before use in restricted environments.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires clear tool design, safe authentication, and useful evaluations. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured workflow for TypeScript or Python MCP integrations.
actual_capabilities: Guides planning for MCP tools, resources, prompts, and transport choices.
Provides TypeScript SDK patterns with Zod schemas and structured outputs.
Provides Python FastMCP patterns with Pydantic models and async API calls.
Explains testing with MCP Inspector, build checks, and syntax checks.
Includes evaluation guidance for realistic read-only question sets.
Includes scripts for connecting to stdio, SSE, or streamable HTTP MCP servers.
limitations: Does not generate a complete production server without service-specific API details.
Requires users to review current MCP SDK documentation before implementation.
Evaluation scripts may run local commands and should only be used with trusted inputs.
Security posture depends on the server code produced by the user and model.

use_cases.title: Create an API-backed MCP server
use_cases.description: Design and implement tools that expose a service API through MCP with clear schemas and useful responses.

use_cases.title: Prepare a local MCP integration
use_cases.description: Build a stdio server for local automation, then test it with inspector and evaluation questions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate server usefulness
use_cases.description: Create realistic read-only tasks and measure whether an AI agent can solve them with the MCP tools.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic MCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP builder skill to plan a small MCP server for my service. Ask me for the API details you need, then propose tools, schemas, and transport.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a TypeScript MCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP builder skill to create a TypeScript MCP server design for this API. Include tool names, Zod schemas, error handling, and build checks.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Python FastMCP server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP builder skill to design a Python FastMCP server for this workflow. Include Pydantic inputs, async API calls, pagination, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create an evaluation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP builder skill to create 10 read-only evaluation questions for this MCP server. Explain how each answer can be verified and what tools the agent should use.

output_examples.input: Plan an MCP server for a project management API.
output: A proposed tool list grouped by workflow and API resource.
Input and output schema guidance for each tool.

output_examples.input: Review my MCP server design for quality.
output: Specific feedback on naming, descriptions, schemas, and error messages.
Testing steps for build, inspector, and representative tool calls.
Suggestions for safer authentication and clearer annotations.

output_examples.input: Create evaluation questions for the server.
output: A set of realistic read-only questions with stable answers.
A verification plan for each expected answer.
Guidance for running and interpreting the evaluation report.

best_practices: Review current MCP protocol and SDK documentation before writing implementation code.
Use strict schemas, clear tool descriptions, and actionable error messages.
Run evaluations only against trusted servers and trusted local commands.
anti_patterns: Do not create vague tools that hide important inputs or side effects.
Do not expose destructive operations without clear annotations and safeguards.
Do not paste real API keys into examples, prompts, or evaluation files.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan, implement, test, and evaluate MCP servers that connect AI tools to external services.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript and Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TypeScript SDK guidance and Python FastMCP guidance with schema and testing patterns.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation, but production readiness requires service details, security review, and real testing.

faq.question: Why does it mention external URLs?
faq.answer: The skill points to MCP protocol and SDK documentation so users can check current APIs and examples.

faq.question: Are the evaluation scripts safe to run?
faq.answer: They are useful for trusted inputs, but they can launch local commands for stdio servers. Review commands before running them.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
